column1:
The FOMC’s May 1, 2019 statement reads mildly dovish/constructive: rates held at 2.25–2.50%, “patience” emphasized with inflation running below 2%, and some cooling in household spending and business investment despite strong labor markets and solid activity. Incorporating the May 2019 Financial Stability Report tempers this tone: the FSR judged overall vulnerabilities as moderate but flagged elevated asset valuations and high nonfinancial business leverage (including leveraged loans/CLOs), even as funding risks remained low and banks well capitalized; equity market volatility had eased from the late‑2018 spike but remained prone to bouts. Together, these FSR insights support a patient, not tightening, stance and nudge the assessment from mildly positive toward cautious‑positive. Adjusted net: slightly positive, but more guarded than the statement alone.
